title: Henry Ford: A Life in Brief
subtitle: He put America on wheels. He also put hatred in print.
creditsLines: Public-domain photographs from the Library of Congress and the Edison and Ford archives,
via Wikimedia Commons; paintings marked Reconstruction are generated, not photographs.
Text checked against: Ford with Crowther, My Life and Work (1922); The Henry Ford archives;
scholarship by Watts, Baldwin and Hounshell. Narration: synthetic voice (ElevenLabs via Magnific).

beats.caption: Reconstruction: a farmhouse kitchen, 1870s
beats.text: Henry Ford was born on a farm near Dearborn, Michigan, in eighteen sixty-three. As a boy, he cared far more about machines than about farm work.

beats.caption: Reconstruction: Detroit, June 1896
beats.text: In eighteen ninety-six, he built his first gasoline-powered vehicle, the Quadricycle. In nineteen oh-three, he started the Ford Motor Company.

beats.caption: Henry Ford, portrait by Hartsook, about 1919
beats.text: The Model T arrived in nineteen oh-eight. It was built for ordinary families, and about fifteen million of them were made.

beats.caption: Assembly line at Highland Park, 1913
beats.text: In nineteen thirteen, his factory began building cars on a moving assembly line. A chassis that once took about twelve and a half hours could be finished in about ninety-three minutes.

beats.caption: Reconstruction: the crowd at the Highland Park gate, January 1914
beats.text: In nineteen fourteen, Ford announced a five-dollar day, far above the usual pay. But to earn the full bonus, workers had to follow his rules about how they lived at home.

beats.caption: Reconstruction: a Dearborn press room, 1920
beats.text: Ford also owned a newspaper, The Dearborn Independent. In nineteen twenty, it began a long series of articles blaming Jewish people for the world's problems. The series used a forged document, and it spread hatred.

beats.caption: Henry Ford at the White House, 1927
beats.text: In nineteen twenty-seven, after a lawsuit, Ford publicly apologized. Historians still disagree about how much he knew of the articles, and what he meant by the apology.

beats.caption: Aerial view of the Ford River Rouge plant
beats.text: At the Rouge plant in nineteen thirty-seven, Ford's security men beat union organizers. Ford did not sign a contract with the union until nineteen forty-one.

beats.caption: Reconstruction: Willow Run bomber plant, 1943
beats.text: In nineteen thirty-eight, Ford accepted a high Nazi honor, the Grand Cross of the German Eagle. Yet in the Second World War, his Willow Run factory built B-24 bombers for the United States.

beats.caption: Henry Ford, 1938
beats.text: Henry Ford died in nineteen forty-seven, at his home, Fair Lane. Historians still disagree about how to weigh his achievements against his hatred, and his treatment of workers.
